linkages: The eIncome register contains the identification number of the employee, which is used to link the monthly payroll data to annual records with additional information about financial wealth (the income-tax register).

sample.universe: All employees in Denmark reported to the eIncome register; the estimation sample is restricted to private-sector employees in two 2008 income bands.
sample.unit_of_observation: individual-month for Fig. 1; individual-year for the Table 1 regressions
selection_rules: 48 consecutive monthly observations from January 2008 to December 2011 with positive wage income.
Contributions to annuity pension schemes of less than DKK 100,000 in 2008 (imposed because deductibility for annuity schemes was capped at DKK 100,000 from 2010).

Allocated to a tax bracket on the basis of income in 2008: treatment group (T-group) = average monthly gross earnings above DKK 35,000 in 2008, roughly the 75th percentile; control group (C-group) = monthly income in the range DKK 30,000-35,000.
Within the T-group, T-group2 = the 4818 individuals whose contribution rate in December 2009 was at least 25 percentage points higher than in December 2008; T-group1 = the rest of the T-group.
sample.period: Monthly data January 2008 - December 2011; annual tax-register data 2006-2011
sample.n_observations: 1,069,320 individual-year observations in the full-sample regressions (Table 1, columns (1) and (3)); 408,702 in the restricted-treatment-group regressions (columns (2) and (4))
sample.n_individuals: 116,724 in the T-group (of whom 4818 in T-group2) and 64,287 in the C-group

construction_notes: Contributions to employer organized and to privately organized pension accounts are measured as a fraction of total annual gross payments to the individual (as a share of total monthly gross payments in Fig. 1).

Savings in financial assets, S, is financial wealth in year t minus financial wealth in year t-1 (the income tax register records financial wealth at the end of the year), expressed relative to total gross payments.
P^TotPen is total contributions to tax subsidized retirement savings accounts, i.e. both employer organized and privately organized accounts, as a fraction of total annual gross payments.

The extraordinary-contributor dummy equals one if the pension contribution rate in December 2009 is 25 percentage points higher than its level in December 2008; footnote 3 reports that results are very similar with other thresholds or with an indicator for extraordinarily high contribution rates in any month after the reform was decided.
P^Empl and P^TotPen are instrumented with the interaction D_{i,2009} x D_i^Treat.

The marginal tax rate for a top taxpayer is computed in footnote 1 as MTR = LMC + (1 - LMC) x (RT + BT + MT + TT + CT) = 8 + (100 - 8) x (32.8 + 5.04 + 6 + 15 + 0.7) = 63% before 1 January 2010 and 8 + (100 - 8) x (32.8 + 3.67 + 0 + 15 + 0.7) = 56% after.
One USD corresponds to around DKK 6.5.
90% of all DC contributions in Denmark are made to employer organized accounts.

identification.source_of_variation: The 2010 Danish tax reform, passed by parliament on 28 May 2009 and taking effect on 1 January 2010, which lowered the marginal tax rate for top-bracket taxpayers from almost 63% to 56% while leaving it practically unchanged for others. Because pension contributions are tax deductible, this created a temporary incentive during the announcement period of 2009 to advance contributions while the deduction rate was still high.

The reform is assumed to leave the control group's marginal tax rate practically unchanged.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The paper states that the reform left the marginal tax rate practically unchanged for people outside the top bracket, and Fig. 1 displays both group series over all 48 months; no formal pre-trend test is reported.

threats_discussed: Fig. 1 documents higher contributions to employer organized pension accounts, but it does not reveal whether this increase is offset by reduced savings in other accounts - the Table 1 regressions are introduced to address this.

The tax deductibility for contributions to annuity schemes was capped at DKK 100,000 from 2010; the sample is restricted to individuals with annuity contributions below DKK 100,000 in 2008 to avoid interference from this rule change.
robustness_checks: Columns (2) and (4) repeat the estimation with the treatment group restricted to the 4818 individuals who made extraordinary contributions to employer organized accounts.

Footnote 3: results are described as very similar using thresholds other than 25 percentage points, or a dummy for extraordinarily high contribution rates in any month after the reform was decided; those results are not shown.
